stories.angle: Two labs shipped open-weight models on the same day at opposite ends of the size spectrum: one memory-native 554B, one ternary 5.9GB that runs on a phone. The story is the pincer, not either model.
facts: MemTensor released and open-sourced MemT-1.0-Pro on 24 November 2026, jointly developed with NVIDIA.
MemT-1.0-Pro is 554 billion total parameters with 59 billion active parameters.
It is built on NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-BF16 as its backbone, trained with NVIDIA Megatron-Core and Megatron Bridge.
Its architecture combines dynamic local memory, which stores information acquired during interaction, with trainable hyper-memory components that learn how to write and read that information.
Scores 41.80 on BEAM-1M versus 37.04 for MemT-1.0-Flash, a 4.76 point improvement.
Scores 23.87 on MemoryAgentBench versus 17.36 for MemT-1.0-Flash, a 6.51 point improvement.
It follows MemTensor's earlier Nano and Flash releases.
PrismML announced Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B on 24 November 2026 from Pasadena, California.
Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B is based on Qwen 3.8 27B, sits at 5.9GB of memory, and uses ternary weights.
Across agentic coding benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified, DeepSWE v1.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1) it averaged 54.2 versus 37.9 for Ternary Bonsai 2 27B.
Across agentic tool-calling benchmarks (AppWorld and tau-3-Bench) it averaged 82.2 versus 60.2 for its predecessor.
It runs on NVIDIA and Intel GPUs through llama.cpp, and on Apple devices including Mac, iPhone and iPad through MLX.
It is released under Apache 2.0 and downloadable free from 24 November 2026.

sources.title: MemTensor Releases and Open-Sources MemT-1.0-Pro, a 554B Memory-Native Model
PrismML Launches Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B for Agentic Coding and Private Knowledge Work

stories.angle: A carmaker's world model that claims to transfer across boats, drones and humanoids. Treat the benchmark claims as company claims, and note why a shared physical-world model matters for robotics.
facts: XPENG unveiled WorldGPT, announced 24 November 2026 in Guangzhou, China.
WorldGPT brings together AI learning across six types of machines: cars, boats, drones, single-arm robots, dual-arm robots and humanoid robots.
The model can predict future scenarios, plan actions and support development of AI systems across different machines.
XPENG says WorldGPT achieved 12 first-place results across public benchmarks in autonomous driving, robotics, visual understanding and video generation.
XPENG says it is the first world model to demonstrate prediction and action-planning capabilities across all six types of machines.
It is developed as part of the XPENG Turing World Model family and is presented as part of XPENG's Physical AI work.

sources.title: XPENG WorldGPT: One Model for Cars, Robots, Drones

stories.angle: Inference silicon is splitting away from training GPUs, and the buyer for the first batch is neoclouds and sovereign clouds. This is the physical layer behind the price war.
facts: SambaNova and Supermicro announced a strategic collaboration, reported 24 November 2026.
The collaboration initially plans for 10,000 SN50 RDU chips from SambaNova.
The systems are disaggregated inference systems that combine RDUs and GPUs, part of Supermicro's Data Center Building Block Solutions portfolio.
Supermicro will integrate, test, deliver and support the systems, including on-site service.
SambaNova engineers will get models running and tuned on SN50 and help Supermicro with deployments.
The companies will start with neoclouds and sovereign clouds, then expand to enterprises running AI in their own data centers.

Charles Liang, president, CEO and CBO of Supermicro, said the collaboration expands the DCBBS portfolio by enabling heterogeneous architectures that integrate GPU computing with specialized inference acceleration.
Rodrigo Liang, cofounder and CEO of SambaNova, said agentic AI is the next wave of inference and has to run everywhere.

sources.title: SambaNova SN50 Chips to Power Supermicro's New Inference Racks

stories.angle: Sovereignty moved from policy language to a shipped product. The air-gapped detail is the one that matters for defence and regulated buyers.
facts: Cloudera announced a digital sovereignty package, reported 24 November 2026.
It combines Anywhere Cloud, Open Data Lakehouse and Unified Data Fabric with open-weight AI models and model customization tools from Mistral AI.
The offering supports deployment across sovereign clouds, private data centers and fully air-gapped environments with no connection to external networks.
Governance policies extend to enterprise data that AI agents retrieve and use while performing tasks.
Mistral's open-weight models can run alongside governed data, letting organizations customize models locally and run agentic workflows without exposing sensitive information.

Cloudera describes its architecture as modular and hybrid, allowing workloads to shift between infrastructure providers and private data centers without rewriting applications or migrating and duplicating underlying data.
Cloudera recently partnered with Mistral AI.

sources.title: Cloudera launches digital sovereignty platform spanning AI and infrastructure

stories.angle: The first public frontier lab posted a record raise and a widening compute bill in the same week. Read the margin, not the debut pop.
facts: Anthropic priced its IPO on 18 November 2026 at $83 per share, above an initial range of $70 to $78.
It sold 980 million shares, up from the 825 million initially indicated.
The offering raised about $81 billion and valued the company at about $1.5 trillion.
Shares began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on 19 November 2026, opening at $111.50, about 34% above the IPO price.
The stock closed its first day at $97.17, about 17% above the IPO price.
It fell about 9% in early trading the following day.
Anthropic's offering produced a valuation of about $2 trillion at its debut, ahead of SpaceX's June listing.
Per its prospectus and reporting on it, compute and infrastructure expense reached 58.2% of revenue in the third quarter of 2026, against 48.1% in the preceding quarter.
That expense was $9,863 million against $16,956 million of third-quarter revenue, versus $5,558 million against $11,555 million in the second quarter.
Anthropic bought $5.0 billion of short-term compute in the third quarter, terms it says currently cost significantly more than multiyear capacity.
The operating result moved from a $974 million profit in the second quarter to a $567 million loss in the third.
The prospectus puts committed compute and lease spending at about $900.9 billion, including $451.6 billion expected before 31 December 2030.
Compute is ordered 12 to 18 months ahead under take-or-pay provisions.
Its nine-month operating loss was $1,260 million, and $19,240 million of training compute sat in research and development.

sources.title: Anthropic's blockbuster debut tests Wall Street's faith in AI boom
Anthropic prices IPO at $83 per share, giving it a $1.5 trillion valuation
OpenAI Cuts GPT-6.2 Astra API Prices as Anthropic's Compute Share Reaches 58%

stories.angle: Google's threat group says the shift from prompting to autonomous multi-agent tooling is the line that got crossed. Concrete, named frameworks and one named victim sector.
facts: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant published the GTIG AI Threat Tracker update on 16 November 2026.
Written by Aurora Blum, Kelli Vanderlee, Jess Xia and David Mainor.
GTIG says adversary tradecraft has moved beyond manual prompting to deploying autonomous multi-agent offensive frameworks.
Named frameworks include ARTEX, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI and PentAGI.
GTIG independently observed open source tools CAIRN and PentAGI deployed in the wild, and has seen experimentation with CyberStrikeAI and HexStrike AI.

CAIRN is an open source, multi-agent pentesting framework that implements an OODA (Observe, Orient, Decide, Act) loop where specialized agents collaborate via a shared blackboard to navigate from an initial parameter such as a target IP address toward an operational objective.
GTIG observed CAIRN used in intrusion activity against targets including in the aerospace sector in the US.

These frameworks share core capabilities: discovering and exploiting low-complexity vulnerabilities, using LLMs to generate single-use payloads on demand, and using real-time execution feedback to dynamically adjust tactics.

Threat actors are increasingly using LLMs and agentic frameworks to automate reverse engineering of patches via differential analysis, letting them weaponize n-day vulnerabilities and scale exploitation pipelines against internet-facing servers without human intervention.

Financially motivated actors profit from LLMJacking by stealing LLM credentials and cloud resources from compromised environments and reselling access through underground proxy services such as LLM Mixers.
State-sponsored groups and commercial Influence-as-a-Service vendors use LLMs to produce synthetic media at scale and automate cross-platform distribution.
Espionage groups use LLMs for target research and novel supply chain vectors, such as manipulating autonomous coding assistant configurations to drop backdoors during local execution.
The report says the adversarial AI landscape has reached a critical inflection point.

sources.title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold
